scientific_verdict: NO_EDGE_VALIDATED (unchanged). Prospective evidence measured here: 26 radar-live alerts = 17 distinct wallet/market/outcome entries; PR #109 evaluator run in memory gives 2 FINAL (one entry, two classes) and 24 PARTIAL. No holdout result.

defect_on_main.what: first_at_or_after returns the first point at or after t with no upper bound
prices-history requested to t0+24h+600 regardless of the evaluation clock
entry and the 1h/6h/24h marks could take a point printed hours later (up to t0+24h+600)

fix_in_pr109.what: first(target, as_of): first point at or after target, rejected if later than min(target+600, as_of)
conflicting prices at one timestamp become None and the mark is withheld
entry and every horizon use the bounded sampler; NOT_YET before maturity

late_mark_defect.status: CLOSED for the defect as defined (unbounded future point selection) — VERIFIED by code reading; measured on 26 live alerts: entry delay 14-142 s, horizon delays 0-122 s, all within 600 s. PR #109 tests were not run here (UNVERIFIED that they pass).

remaining_post_alert_paths.what: Wallet history is the NEWEST 1,000 /v2/activity rows read when the entry is evaluated, which can be hours after the trade (radar-live: 17 of 26 alerts emitted 13259-50524 s after trigger). Rows dated after t push earlier rows out of the window; first_seen is set only when has_more is false (line 296) and a floor of 1000 is substituted (line 290). So the wallet's post-trigger activity changes prior_trades, age_h, THIN and R1 inputs. asof.view itself filters strictly before t (asof.py:28-50), so the leak is through truncation, not through reading future rows.

Address code, nonce and public tags are read at fetch time (present-day) and used to exclude links/payers. Documented as exclusion-only, but it is post-alert information deciding which alerts survive. historical_addresses (block-specific) exists for some reads.

Gamma tags, family and end_ts are read when a token is first resolved (during catch-up, after t) and stored once; hours_to_end feature and the END_GRACE admissibility rule use that value. A later revision of the scheduled end or tags can enter. UNVERIFIED how often Gamma revises these.

Semantics of a prices-history point (instant vs bucket summarising up to fidelity=60 s after t) are not documented in the repo; if bucketed forward, the entry mark could include up to ~60 s of post-emission trades. Not tested.
Raw Gamma and prices-history responses are not hashed or stored with the evaluation; a later re-fetch may differ (backfill, revision), so a mark cannot be re-verified.

Label is the latest Gamma state at evaluation time; closedTime<=now gate (line 67) is vacuous in live use because now is the real clock. Labels are meant to be post-alert; risk is only label revision (UMA dispute) without a sealed copy.

FINAL requires a resolved label AND all three marks. A market that resolves within 24 h of emission loses its later chart points, so it never becomes FINAL. Measured: alert 98ff58e62b7310bf2b8feda3 (market closed 6473 s after emission, outcome lost) has 6h/24h marks None and stays PARTIAL. An analysis restricted to FINAL conditions on resolution timing.

Shadow return buys at the chart price (no spread) with one flat fee (default 0.0) although 20 of 26 alert markets have feesEnabled with rate 0.01 or 0.05 (live_alerts_close_vs_emission.json). Returns are overstated.

Cutoffs are correct (observed_at<=emitted, public_at<=received<=reviewed, body sha256 and evidence id re-derived). But every clock is the archive's own; nothing is independently timestamped. Context output is not used by features, alerts, marks or labels (radar/__main__.py@PR:151-154 prints it only). Coverage measured: 3 public_milestone rows, last observed 1793130745, none during the radar-live run.

selection_on_outcome.live_scores: M1 rarity is fitted on a discovery population with no outcome (models.py:1-8, enrich.py:333-339, threshold from phi_engine/reference/rarity_discovery.json.gz). M3 edge_fit reads outcomes (models.py:6,98) but is called only in models.py:153-156 inside the synthetic self-test; no caller in enrich.py or __main__.py (grep). VERIFIED.
selection_on_outcome.classes: C1-C7 and R1 come from the frozen study (asof.py:1-12; enrich.py:22 'phase-8 S_FRESH'). Whether those definitions were derived from retrospectively identified winning wallets was not checked here (UNVERIFIED: requires the frozen study plan). The study's own out-of-sample result is embedded in each alert (e.g. R1 NOT_SUPPORTED_EFFECT_EXCLUDED, excess -0.0597, CI [-0.103, -0.016]).
selection_on_outcome.pr109_research: PR #109 PROTOCOL.md says published Nobel and sports results were known before the plan and the tests are retrospective; DISCOVERY_PROTOCOL.md says the extension was defined after seeing the three reconciled intermediaries (exploratory). No tuning of radar thresholds on those cases was found in radar/ or phi_engine/ (grep), VERIFIED only for those directories.
